transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-18 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CSM), Mark Donovan (CISO, Celestia), Leila Park (Security Analyst), Samir Patel (Cloud Engineer), Naomi Brooks (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE, this is Priya SE, Carlos is on for CSM. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Mark Donovan: Good thanks. busy but ready. we sent over the SIG earlier today, so hoping to walk through and see what evidence you can provide.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Yup, that's the plan. We'll go section by section and flag anything that needs a deeper dive. Priya, want to kick off?
[00:28] Priya Natarajan: Sure. I'll share my screen with the SIG spreadsheet in a sec. Also quick callout: we've got SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation ready to share, plus a pen test summary and our audit log retention policy.
[00:41] Leila Park: Awesome. For Celestia, top items are KMS ownership, data residency, audit logs exportability, and SSO/RBAC scoping. We also need to confirm retention windows for logs.
[00:51] Priya Natarajan: Totally get it. On KMS we support both Redwood-managed keys and customer-managed keys via KMS integrations. Currently we have KMS integrations with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. If you need an HSM-backed customer key, we can discuss options for Private deployments.
[01:10] Samir Patel: Clarify "customer-managed" — does that mean keys never leave our KMS? how do you handle envelope encryption and tokenization?
[01:19] Priya Natarajan: Good question. With customer-managed keys (CMK) in a VPC/private setup, Redwood never persists plaintext keys. We do envelope encryption: service encrypts with a data key that is itself wrapped by your CMK. For hosted deployments we can also offer Bring-Your-Own-Key via KMS but there are additional controls around key rotation and logs.
[01:39] Mark Donovan: we need to see the cryptographic architecture diagram and key rotation policy. also the KMS access logs.
[01:47] Jordan Lee: We'll attach the crypto architecture diagram and our key rotation policy to the SIG evidence. Priya will include the KMS integration notes and sample logs.
[01:56] Leila Park: On RBAC and SSO, can you do SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning? We want to map AD groups to roles.
[02:06] Priya Natarajan: Yes, SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning is supported. We map SCIM groups to RBAC roles in the Console, and you can customize role permissions. There is an audit log for admin actions and role changes.
[02:20] Naomi Brooks: Is RBAC enforced at the API level as well? we need to lock down service account keys.
[02:26] Priya Natarajan: API keys respect RBAC roles, and service accounts can be scoped. For stricter controls we recommend using short‑lived tokens with our token broker and integrating with your identity provider.
[02:38] Samir Patel: Any built-in separation of duties? Like can we restrict who can create models vs who can deploy?
[02:44] Priya Natarajan: Absolutely, roles are granular. Typical separation: model management, deployment admin, billing view, and security admin. We can share the role matrix.
[02:54] Jordan Lee: We'll attach the role matrix and a sample SCIM user/role mapping.
[03:00] Mark Donovan: moving on to audit logs — retention, export and tamper evidence. We need 365+ days retention and offsite export to our S3 bucket.
[03:12] Priya Natarajan: Our hosted API retains audit logs for 365 days by default for enterprise plans; we can extend retention for Dedicated/Private. Exports: we support periodic export to customer S3 via a signed transfer or you can pull via our audit log export API. Tamper evidence: logs are integrity-signed; we can provide the format and verification steps.
[03:33] Leila Park: Do you provide a chain of custody or feed into our SIEM?
[03:37] Priya Natarajan: Yes, we can stream logs to your SIEM via Kinesis/CloudWatch/ PubSub or push to S3. We'll include example ingestion configs.
[03:47] Mark Donovan: Data residency — our underwriting data must remain in EU region. Can we pin model serving to eu-west-1 and prevent fallback to other regions?
[03:58] Jordan Lee: Yes, you can pin region-level routing. For Hosted we have options to restrict to specific regions; for strict requirements we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated in your preferred region. We also support region pinning policies that prevent cross-region fallback.
[04:16] Samir Patel: If we go Private, are we able to run totally air-gapped? and what about model updates/patching?
[04:22] Priya Natarajan: For Private on-prem installations, we support air-gapped deployments. Model updates would be handled via signed artifacts shipped through your release process. We can provide update manifests and verification signatures.
[04:36] Leila Park: On SOC 2 and ISO, you said you'd share attestation. Are there any major control exceptions we should be aware of?
[04:43] Priya Natarajan: No exceptions in the latest audit; SOC 2 Type II covers the security criteria and ISO 27001 certificate is current. We'll send the formal reports — they contain the scope and dates.
[04:55] Naomi Brooks: procurement will need liability and indemnity language, plus a DPA. We may need a data processing addendum with specific residency clauses.
[05:03] Jordan Lee: Understood. We'll coordinate legal and bring a template DPA. Carlos, can you own that thread?
[05:08] Carlos Mendez: Yep, I'll follow up with procurement and share our standard DPA and redlines we've accepted previously.
[05:14] Mark Donovan: For the SIG answers, a lot of the questions ask for specific evidence like config screenshots, policy docs, and penetration test reports. What's the usual way you provide that?
[05:24] Priya Natarajan: We typically populate the SIG spreadsheet with our answers and attach links to evidence in a secured S3 bucket or SharePoint link, with access restrictions. For sensitive artifacts we can provide redacted versions and allow an NDA/secure exchange if needed.
[05:38] Leila Park: Example: Q: key management — ask for proof that keys are customer-controlled. We'd want sample KMS access logs showing only our principal used the unwrapping call.
[05:48] Priya Natarajan: We'll surface a sample access log and the KMS audit trail as part of the evidence set. For hosted customers it's typically audit log slices with tenant IDs redacted as needed. For Dedicated/Private we can provide fuller logs.
[06:02] Samir Patel: Anything about data plane encryption at rest and in transit? we need cipher suites and TLS versions.
[06:09] Priya Natarajan: We use TLS 1.2+ and recommend 1.3; cipher suites are modern ECDHE-based. At rest we use AES-256, with envelope encryption for customer data. We'll attach the crypto spec.
[06:21] Jordan Lee: quick check — do you need vulnerability scan reports or the pen test summary?
[06:26] Mark Donovan: yes, pen test summary and a high level of the vulnerability management program. also patch cadence for infra.
[06:33] Priya Natarajan: We'll include the pen test executive summary and our vuln mgmt policy: weekly CVE triage, monthly patch windows for noncritical, emergency patches as needed.
[06:44] Leila Park: On segmentation, can we limit egress to a whitelist of destinations? we don't want models to call out to external endpoints.
[06:52] Priya Natarajan: Yes, egress controls via outbound firewall rules are supported in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted we offer outbound allow/deny lists and rate-limiting; full blocking is available in Private.
[07:06] Samir Patel: About ephemeral KV caches — do they persist across host reboots? what's the retention?
[07:12] Priya Natarajan: KV cache is in-memory for performance; for warm start we persist encrypted checkpoints to disk with lifecycle controls. In private deployments you control retention and deletion. We'll include the cache lifecycle doc.
[07:27] Jordan Lee: we should call out typical redwood evidence artifacts: SOC2, ISO, pen test summary, role matrix, SCIM/SAML config examples, network diagram, KMS integration notes, audit log export sample. We'll populate the SIG with direct links to those.
[07:41] Mark Donovan: Great. There are a few SIG rows we'll want to mark as "needs follow-up" — multi-tenant data separation, KMS proof, and audit export format.
[07:50] Priya Natarajan: Noted, we'll flag those and schedule deeper technical calls on any unresolved items.
[07:58] Naomi Brooks: From procurement, timeline is roughly two weeks for initial legal review and another two for internal approvals. We may request contract amendments around data residency.
[08:08] Jordan Lee: That aligns with our experience. We'll aim to have the SIG evidence and docs over by Friday.
[08:14] Leila Park: One last technical: how do you handle model rollbacks and auditability when a model causes a quality regression? we need traceability per request.
[08:24] Priya Natarajan: We keep model version metadata per request in the audit logs; you can trace request -> model version + parameters. Rollbacks are via deployment control plane with canary options and immutable model versions. We'll include the rollout and rollback docs.
[08:40] Samir Patel: For the network diagram review, can we do a short follow-up with our infra team and your SEs?
[08:46] Priya Natarajan: Yes, propose 30-minute slot next week; we'll do a deep dive into VPC peering, route tables, and NAT/egress.
[08:55] Jordan Lee: OK, quick recap of action items and next steps — we'll fill the SIG, attach the evidence, send SOC 2/ISO, share role matrix and SCIM examples, schedule the network diagram review, and Carlos will start procurement DPA thread.
[09:10] Mark Donovan: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:13] Naomi Brooks: Thanks, talk soon.
[09:15] Jordan Lee: Thanks all.

End of transcript.
